coordinate_contract: The liquid field and the displacement are computed in the SOP's object space, in units of Flow size (the object's radius in SOP units) measured from Flow centre, then go through TDDeform (positions) and TDDeformNorm (normals), so object transforms, non-uniform scale and instances apply after the motion; a zero normal stays zero (decided before TDDeformNorm); the rebuilt normal keeps the rest normal only where the moved patch is squeezed to under a thousandth of its rest area (a fold) or is NaN. Gravity is given in world space and brought into object space with uTDMats[].worldInverse and the inverse of TDInstanceMat3(), so it stays world-down for rotated instances. Flow time is Flow speed added up per frame in Python (presets.advance(), double precision) and wrapped at 25600; the shader folds every noise drift into one 256-cell repeat of its lattice. The pixel stage is the Liquid Glass contract: world-space normals, eye and light; camera-space refraction offset projected with the camera's own projection and the measured screen orientation (screenSign); screen UV from gl_FragCoord and uTDGeneral.viewport (TD texture convention, v up); distances along the view ray (Euclidean for perspective, depth for orthographic cameras); ripples and film looked up at the rest position (object space) times the Geometry COMP's world scale (worldScale()), so they stick to the object and count in world-sized steps (uPhase drift, 256-unit lattice), ripple slope rescaled so Wobble does not depend on that scale; screen orientation measured per pixel (projected against raster position, the projected position's screen derivative on a centre-line tie); equirectangular panorama in this study's convention (u = 0 toward +X, then +Z), not yet compared natively. Two sizes, one job each. Flow size (SOP units, the demo sphere = 1) scales the motion, which happens before TDDeform. Object size follows the Liquid Glass family rule (Liquid Glass Lit decisions.json, family_rule): the object's world radius over 1.45, the core's demo torus. It multiplies Thickness and Frost and divides Tint density, Wobble scale and the film swirl frequency; with worldScale() in the pattern lookups, the glass looks the same whether the object is sized in its SOP or by its Geometry COMP. Fit to Glass geometry sets both from the same object.
color_contract: Colour parameters are artistic values passed as data vectors. Colour parameters (Auto) follows project.workingColorSpace: pass-through keeps them as typed; a linear working space converts them from sRGB to linear in the shader (transfer curve only, no gamut conversion). Output is premultiplied alpha; the material blends with One / One Minus Source Alpha. The back-face pass is a data texture (rgba32float, alpha = distance) read with texelFetch.
